sections.html:
• Scientific name: Megalancistrus barrae (Steindachner, 1910)
  • Common names: Black Spiny Ashiura Pleco, Azzura Pleco, Giant Ancistrus
  • Type locality: Rio São Francisco near Barra, Brazil.
  • Synonym: Ancistrus barrae
  • Size: 385 mm (15.2") SL
  • Etymology: Greek, megas, megalos = great + Greek, agkistron = hook, in this case meaning "big Ancistrus". Named for the Rio São Francisco near Barra in Brazil, the type locality.
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2018).

Family: Loricariidae. Common name: Black Spiny Ashiura Pleco. Synonym: Ancistrus barrae. Size: 38.5 cm. Temperature: 20-27°C. pH: 6.0-7.5.

Megalancistrus is closely related to Pseudacanthicus. In both sexes the body is covered in spiny odontodes, but Megalancistrus has more soft rays in the dorsal fin (10 to 12).
South America: São Francisco River basin, Brazil.

South America: São Francisco River basin, Brazil. Type locality: Rio São Francisco near Barra, Brazil. Megalancistrus barrae occurs in the lower and middle São Francisco River, where it is infrequent and not very abundant. This is probably due in part to the difficulty of capturing it. No significant threats to the species were detected, so it is categorised as Least Concern (LC) (IUCN 2022).
Needs a very large aquarium as it is a territorial species. It also needs hiding places such as driftwood and large caves.
Omnivore. Frozen foods such as brine shrimp, mosquito larvae, shrimps, mussels and fish flesh, as well as good quality dried foods. They will also eat green foods in the aquarium.
Males have a broader head, longer pectoral fins and a slender body, and the odontodes are longer, especially around the gill cover area.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.

A colossal pleco worthy of the generic name. Can be differentiated from other large loricariids by the presence of evertible interopercular odontodes.

This species' background colour is dark brown to black; those more commonly exported are black, and often they are exported under the nomen nudem "Megalancistrus etentaculatus".
Etymology: the specific name barrae refers to the Rio São Francisco near Barra in Brazil, the species' type locality.
